grammarPoints.title: Comparing two choices
grammarPoints.meaning: Say which of two things has more of a quality, or ask which one does.
grammarPoints.formation: A のほうが B より adjective です. Question: A と B と、どちらのほうが adjective ですか.
notes: のほうが identifies the higher side and より the comparison standard; word order may change without reversing the meaning.
The adjective itself does not get a special comparative ending. どっち is a more conversational alternative to どちら.

examples.english: The white bag is smaller than the red bag.
examples.japanese: 白いかばんのほうが赤いかばんより小さいです。
examples.kana: しろいかばんのほうがあかいかばんよりちいさいです。

schemas.context: Compare the two named items in a shop.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Compare distinct physical objects on the same dimension. The truth is supplied by the English prompt.

schemas.japanese: {a}と{b}と、どちらのほうが{quality}ですか。
schemas.kana: {a}と{b}と、どちらのほうが{quality}ですか。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Exactly two alternatives are being compared. Do not use いちばん here.

grammarPoints.title: Choosing the most from a group
grammarPoints.meaning: Identify the highest degree of a quality among three or more choices.
grammarPoints.formation: Group の中で、item がいちばん adjective です. Ask with the suitable question word + がいちばん.
notes: Use どれ for a visible list of items, 何 for many category questions, だれ for people, どこ for places, and いつ for times.
For three or more choices, do not replace the superlative pattern with どっち or のほう.

examples.english: Among these hats, the red hat is the largest.
examples.japanese: 帽子の中で、赤い帽子がいちばん大きいです。
examples.kana: ぼうしのなかで、あかいぼうしがいちばんおおきいです。

schemas.context: At least three items of this category are on display.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The selected item must belong to the group. There must be three or more alternatives in context.

schemas.context: You can see at least three items of the stated category.
schemas.japanese: {group}の中で、どれがいちばん{quality}ですか。
schemas.kana: {group}のなかで、どれがいちばん{quality}ですか。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use どれ because the alternatives are visible things, not people or places.

grammarPoints.title: Replacing a known noun with の
grammarPoints.meaning: Avoid repeating a thing already identified: “the small one,” “the clean one,” or “Aki’s.”
grammarPoints.formation: I-adjective + の; na-adjective + な + の; possessor noun + の.
notes: The missing noun must be recoverable from context. In ordinary descriptions of people, use 人 rather than this “one” pattern.
Possessive の appears just once: あきさんの, not あきさんのの.

examples.english: I will buy the small one.
examples.kana: ちいさいのをかいます。

schemas.context: You have been comparing two bags. Avoid repeating “bag.”
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: の replaces a known inanimate object. Keep the final い.

schemas.context: You have been comparing two rooms. Avoid repeating “room.”
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Keep な before the replacement の. The referent is a room.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The person owns the bag. Do not add a second の or repeat かばん after の.

grammarPoints.title: Intentions with つもり
grammarPoints.meaning: Describe an intention to do or avoid an action. A past form describes an earlier plan.
grammarPoints.formation: Nonpast short verb + つもりです; nonpast negative + つもりです. Earlier plan: verb + つもりでした.
notes: Keep the action verb nonpast even when the intention is past.
A plan is stronger than simply wondering about an action. Use a controllable action and a person who can intend it.

examples.english: I intend to exercise on Sunday.
examples.japanese: 日曜日に運動するつもりです。
examples.kana: にちようびにうんどうするつもりです。

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use a controllable action in its dictionary form. The day is in the future.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Negate the action before つもり. The intention itself is present.

schemas.context: Describe last week’s plan, which you did not carry out.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Past tense belongs on でした; do not put a past verb before つもり.

grammarPoints.title: Becoming different: なる
grammarPoints.meaning: Describe a change of state, degree, or role.
grammarPoints.formation: I-adjective: remove い and add くなる. Na-adjective or noun: add になる. Conjugate なる for time and politeness.
notes: Do not say 大きいになる. いい becomes よくなる.
A change can be absolute or relative. 前より explicitly compares with before.

examples.japanese: 教室は静かになりました。
examples.kana: きょうしつはしずかになりました。

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The selected physical place can become larger or smaller. Use く, not に, with the i-adjective.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use a room quality and に before なる.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: A person can enter the occupation; use noun + に.

grammarPoints.title: Somewhere, someone, and their negatives
grammarPoints.meaning: Refer to an unspecified place or person, or say that none was involved.
grammarPoints.formation: どこかに / だれかに with an affirmative or question; どこにも / だれにも with a negative predicate.
notes: Particles such as に, へ, and で follow か but come before negative も: どこかで / どこでも + negative.
In these basic patterns, 何か and 何も do not need を. Negative も requires a negative predicate.

examples.english: I did not go anywhere on Saturday.
examples.japanese: 土曜日はどこにも行きませんでした。
examples.kana: どようびはどこにもいきませんでした。

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Destination に follows どこか. This is an open question, not a negative assertion.

schemas.english: I did not go anywhere on {day}.
schemas.japanese: {day}はどこにも行きませんでした。
schemas.kana: {day}はどこにもいきませんでした。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use どこにも with a negative motion verb; not どこもに.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: 会う marks the person met with に. Keep that に after だれか.

schemas.english: I did not meet anyone on {day}.
schemas.japanese: {day}はだれにも会いませんでした。
schemas.kana: {day}はだれにもあいませんでした。
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Preserve 会う’s に before も and make the verb negative.

grammarPoints.title: Means, tools, and language with で
grammarPoints.meaning: Name the means of transport, tool, medium, or language used to do something.
grammarPoints.formation: Means noun + で + action. The destination still takes に or へ; an object still takes を.
notes: A location can also take で, but here で answers “by what means?”
“On foot” is 歩いて, not a transport noun plus で. Match tools to actions they can perform.

examples.english: I wrote my name with a pencil.
examples.japanese: 鉛筆で名前を書きました。
examples.kana: えんぴつでなまえをかきました。

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: Use transport vehicles that can reach these local destinations. Do not generate 歩いてで.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The tool must be suitable for writing and the object must be writable.

schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: で marks the language used, while と marks the conversation partner.

grammarPoints.title: Extra: do something and come back
grammarPoints.meaning: Use てくる when an action happens elsewhere and is followed by movement toward the current location.
grammarPoints.formation: Verb te-form + 来る; polite nonpast 〜てきます, past 〜てきました.
notes: Context must establish a return or movement toward the speaker’s reference location.
This introductory use is physical movement; do not generate later abstract “has begun to” meanings.

examples.english: I will go buy milk and come back.
examples.kana: ぎゅうにゅうをかってきます。

schemas.context: You are at home, about to go to a shop and return home.
schemas.english: I will go buy {item} and come back.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The action is buying a portable item elsewhere and returning here.

schemas.context: You have returned home with the purchase.
schemas.english: I went and bought {item} and came back.
schemas.omission: The understood speaker or topic may be omitted; retain the information requested.
restrictions: The past ending applies to 来る; the buying verb stays in te-form.

grammarPoints.title: Extra: leaving room for a reply with が or けど
grammarPoints.meaning: End with が or けど to offer relevant information and invite the other person to respond.
grammarPoints.formation: Polite sentence + が…; conversational sentence + けど….
notes: The unfinished ending can soften a request or let the listener choose. It need not mean a strong contradiction.
Provide a conversational opening in the scenario so that the incomplete ending has a purpose.

examples.english: I am free in the afternoon…

schemas.context: Someone is arranging a meeting. Offer this information politely, ending with が and leaving room for their suggestion.
schemas.omission: The request or suggestion is left implicit for the listener to supply.
restrictions: This is intentionally an unfinished conversational turn. Do not force an unrelated contrasting clause.

schemas.context: A close friend is arranging a meeting. End casually with けど and leave room for their suggestion.
schemas.omission: The request or suggestion is left implicit for the listener to supply.
restrictions: Retain だ after 暇 before けど. The unfinished turn invites a response.
